Page base links

This article explains how to use the guide and its examples. Read the Templates, return to the Root, or jump to the Fragment. Each destination belongs to this synthetic documentation page.

The browser resolves relative addresses using the effective document base. A guide can live in a different directory from the current page, so its illustrations and related pages must use that base consistently. The original page address still identifies the source of the article.

Examples and results

Follow the templates to create a small document and inspect the diagram to understand its structure. The root link opens a page outside the assets directory. The fragment identifies this section and remains useful when readers move through the converted document.

These examples use static local markup and reserved example addresses. They need no remote resources during conversion. Enough explanatory prose surrounds the links for article extraction to retain the complete example and its image.
